findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that `_blame_file_commits` must change its return type to `list[str] | None` (returning `None` on git failure, `[]` on success with no lines) so `derive_caused_by` can reliably detect per-path failure vs. legitimate empty output.
evidence: `_blame_file_commits` line 71: `if out is None: return []` — failure is indistinguishable from empty-file success at the call site
Plan AC: 'derive_caused_by returns None when _blame_file_commits fails for any path' — implies derive_caused_by can detect failure, but the current return type (list[str]) cannot express it
ABSENCE: plan never mentions changing _blame_file_commits's return type or contract from list[str] to list[str] | None
findings.finding: _blame_file_commits currently returns [] for BOTH a git failure (line 71: `if out is None: return []`) AND a legitimate empty file (no lines parsed from successful git output). The plan's fix — 'abort on any per-path blame failure' — cannot be implemented correctly without first changing _blame_file_commits's return contract to return None on failure vs. [] on success-with-no-lines. Without that prerequisite change, an implementer treating [] as failure would incorrectly abort on empty files; treating [] as success leaves the bug unfixed. The plan specifies only the derive_caused_by behavior and does not mention this required change to the helper's signature.
findings.location: Code fix section / src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:67-71 (_blame_file_commits) and derive_caused_by loop at :109
scenarios: Implementer follows plan literally, treats [] return as failure, and inadvertently aborts derive_caused_by for bugs whose file_impact includes any legitimately-empty file (e.g., an __init__.py with no content).
Implementer treats [] as success (no change to _blame_file_commits), writes the abort condition in derive_caused_by incorrectly, and the partial-tally bug remains.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Files/code-fix section: '_blame_file_commits signature changes to `-> list[str] | None`; it returns `None` when `_git` returns `None` (any git/OS failure) and `[]` when git succeeds but the file has no lines. `derive_caused_by` checks `if _blame_file_commits(...) is None: return None`.' The AC unit-test injecting a per-path failure should inject a None return from _blame_file_commits (not []) to keep the empty-file case as a separate passing scenario.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `log.warning` (or equivalent metric/trace) in `derive_caused_by` whenever it aborts early due to a per-path blame failure, naming the failing path and the reason, so operators can distinguish 'blame unavailable on blobless clone' from 'bug genuinely has no culprit'.
evidence: Plan states 'Total failure is benign (blame.py:37 returns None)' and the fix 'returns None when _blame_file_commits fails for any path' — no mention of logging or instrumentation in either the fix description or the ACs.
ABSENCE: No AC or implementation note requires a log.warning / metric increment on the abort path.
findings.finding: When `derive_caused_by` aborts because a per-path blame fails, no log line, metric, or trace is emitted. Operators and developers running on blobless clones will silently lose `caused_by` attribution with no observable signal to diagnose why.
scenarios: A user on a blobless clone runs a bug-close transition; caused_by is silently omitted; the user has no way to know blame failed and no operator alert fires.
A partial object-store warm-up occurs intermittently; derive_caused_by flips between aborting and succeeding with no trace, making the root cause of missing attributions invisible.
findings.suggested_fix: In the new early-return branch in `derive_caused_by`, emit: `logger.warning('derive_caused_by: aborting partial blame — path %s failed; returning None (blobless clone?)', failing_path)` before returning None.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a docstring comment to `derive_caused_by` (and/or an entry in AGENTS.md / a design note in `docs/`) explaining why a per-path blame failure causes a full abort rather than a partial tally, referencing the blobless-clone partial-warm scenario.
evidence: Plan explains the rationale well ('strict-majority test runs over a subset and can elect a culprit that would not have won over the full set') but this reasoning lives only in the plan/commit message, not in the codebase or a linked design doc.
ABSENCE: No AC or Files entry requires updating AGENTS.md, an ADR, or the function's docstring with the abort-on-partial rationale.
findings.finding: The behavioral contract change to `derive_caused_by` — abort on any per-path failure rather than tally over the partial set — is a novel policy decision that is not captured in any persistent design artifact (AGENTS.md, an ADR, or an inline docstring explaining the rationale). Future maintainers may revert or weaken this policy without understanding why it was introduced.
scenarios: A future contributor sees the early-return and 'simplifies' it back to partial tallying, reintroducing the wrong-answer bug.
A code reviewer unfamiliar with blobless-clone semantics questions why blame failure is fatal rather than advisory and relaxes the check.
